title: Grammar in Real Communication

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to integrate the Unit language to complete a sustained C1 mission about advanced grammar in context. The central language focus is integrated advanced grammar review. In the context of advanced grammar in context, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At C1, precision includes stance, register, and information structure. Make the relationship between claims explicit, qualify what cannot be fully supported, and adapt the wording to the audience without losing nuance.

blocks.english: This example illustrates rarely have I clearly.
blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.

blocks.english: We should consider what matters most is carefully.
blocks.explanation: This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “This example illustrates rarely have I clearly.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “We should consider what matters most is carefully.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: integrated advanced grammar review. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by integrated advanced grammar review; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For grammar in real communication, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction. This sixth Lesson consolidates Lessons 1–5 and introduces no major new grammar. Select among the Unit patterns according to the communicative need.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.

stages.title: Listen for meaning and stance
stages.instructions: Listen first, then reveal the text and notice connections, register, and emphasis.

segments.text: To begin with, This example illustrates rarely have I clearly. We should consider what matters most is carefully.
In this situation, We should consider what matters most is carefully. The discussion highlighted under no circumstances.
From another perspective, The discussion highlighted under no circumstances. A clear explanation addresses grammatical emphasis directly.
More specifically, A clear explanation addresses grammatical emphasis directly. The speaker emphasized information flow.
Even so, The speaker emphasized information flow. Our response should account for assuming that.
As a result, Our response should account for assuming that. This example illustrates on condition that clearly.
On reflection, This example illustrates on condition that clearly. We should consider but for carefully.
